questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

The burning sun

X-our very 

Y-seemed to be sucking

Z-blood out of us
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: YXZ**

‘The burning sun’ is the subject of the sentence and must be doing some action. Thus, it must be followed by a verb (in active voice). Y comes first. Then it is followed by X, which begins to introduce the object. Z comes third. Thus, the sentence is: The burning sun seemed to be sucking our very blood out of us.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

The tutor always answers the students' questions.

options.text: The students' questions is always answered by the tutor
Questions answered by the tutor are by the students
The students' questions are always answered by the tutor
Questions answered by the tutor is by the students

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: The students' questions are always answered by the tutor.**

Here, the subject is the tutor and the object is the 'students’ questions’. The verb 'answers’ must be replaced by 'are answered’. In the passive voice, the object is acted upon by the subject. Therefore the sentence is: The students’ questions are always answered by the tutor.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

I hear the sound

X-his tool raised 

Y-of the blow while I see 

Z-above his head
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: YXZ**

'Sound’ is followed by the preposition 'of’. Y begins with of and is therefore the first phrase. Y is followed by X as logically 'while I see his tool raised’ makes sense. Then comes Z which starts with the preposition 'above’ which fits perfectly after 'raised’. The sentence is: I hear the sound of the blow while I see his tool raised above his head.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

Mother said, "Will you tell me what it means, Pritam?"

options.text: Mother asked Pritam if he will tell her what it meant
Mother asked Pritam that he would tell her what it meant
Mother asked Pritam if he would tell her what it meant
Mother asked Pritam that he will tell her what it meant

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- __**Mother asked Pritam if he would tell her what it meant**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**​

 
• Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from direct to indirect speech:
 
• The tense of direct speech is changed only when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• When the direct speech is in an interrogative form, we follow the steps given below:
 
 
• The reporting verb said to is converted into asked.
 
• Connectors 'whether' or 'if' are used in place of comma and inverted commas.
 
• Change the reported speech from interrogative to assertive.
 
• The personal pronouns will be changed according to the subject and object of the reporting verb.
 
• ​Here the 2nd person 'you' will change into the 3rd person 'he' as per the object.
 
• Similarly 'me' is converted into 'her' as per the subject.
 
• The auxiliary verb (will) in direct speech changes to (would).
 
• **Present Indefinite tense **is changed into **past indefinite tense. (means-meant)**
 
 
 
• ​At last line up the remaining part.

 
 
• 
 
Following these steps, we finally get- *Mother asked Pritam if he would tell her what it meant*

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

The shepherd guarded a large ________ of sheep and allowed them to move from pasture to pasture.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

We might (have doing) something to help you.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: have done**

'Might have’ is used to show something that has probably happened in the past. In this sentence, there is a possibility that help had been offered in the past. Therefore, the sentence must be: We might have helped you in the past.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Facsimile​
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: Replica**

‘Facsimile’ means an extra copy.

'Disparate’ is to describe something that is not easily comparable.

**'Replica’ is the exact copy of something.**

'Peculiar’ means strange.

'Contrast’ means strikingly different.

Thus, 'replica’ is closest in meaning to 'facsimile’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

The fun ____________ reduced significantly when mom decided to tag along.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: quotient**

A quotient is used as a degree or measure of something (generally intangible). The higher the quotient, the higher the degree. In this sentence, 'quotient’ fits perfectly and the meaning implied is that the degree of fun was reduced. 'Sign’ is a mark or signal that communicates information. 'Moment’ is a subjective measure of time.

He (to be) positively rude.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: was being**
